clue.text: Bit of material in old paper probed by female copper

indicators.note: being probed means having something pushed inside, so the paper's letters take the next pieces into their middle

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
Cu is the chemical symbol for the metal copper

explanation.surface: A scrap of fabric is tucked inside an old newspaper being examined by a policewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer, but here it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover scrap trimmed from a larger piece of cloth or timber is exactly this kind of remnant.

clue.text: A Liberal party led by strong Nick?

indicators.note: being led by means the strong piece goes in front of the rest

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical marking for loud or strong
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in British politics
a do is an informal word for a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Liberal party is headed by a strong man called Nick.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Faldo is an English golfer who won six major championships; the question mark warns that the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is the first name of the famous English golfer with this surname, a definition by example.

clue.text: Group that's bound to work together

definitions.text: Group that's bound to work together

parts.words: Group that's bound to work together
parts.note: reads as a committed team, but describes convicts literally chained to one another while labouring

explanation.definitionFit: Prisoners shackled together for outdoor hard labour formed such a gang, literally bound to work side by side.

clue.text: Country outing — nothing to be missed — essential

indicators.note: something missed out is left out, so the round letter is dropped from the outing word

parts.note: a tour is an outing or trip
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing
key as an adjective means essential or crucial

explanation.surface: An excursion to the countryside where nothing can be skipped is a must.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be missed' removes the round letter standing for nothing from the outing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is a nation spanning south-eastern Europe and western Asia.

clue.text: Helpless person made lax when coming into fortune

indicators.note: coming into means entering, so the rearranged letters go inside the fortune word

parts.note: luck is another word for fortune

indicators.note: lax means loose or slack, signalling that the letters of made are loosely rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who inherits a fortune becomes idle and useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Helpless person' is the whole definition; 'lax' is the anagram signal, not part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an ineffectual person or a politician whose power has drained away.

clue.text: Demand for total affection coming from man mowing with partner?

definitions.text: Demand for total affection coming from man mowing with partner?

parts.words: Demand for total affection coming from man mowing with partner?
parts.note: the saying asks that a person be accepted together with everything that belongs to them; the nursery song has one man go to mow with his dog

explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the counting song 'One man went to mow, went to mow a meadow... and his dog'; the man would say this proverb about his canine partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb insists that anyone who cares for you must also accept your faults and attachments.

clue.text: Damage on jewellery that gives a streaky appearance

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Scratches on gaudy jewellery leave streaks on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative finish of veined, swirling colour imitates the stone used for statues, giving a streaked effect.

clue.text: Would a chap keep this country house? Yes!

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the answer sits inside the words of the clue

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a man would keep a rural home, and answers yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian second home in the countryside, often a summer cottage, goes by this name.

clue.text: University participating in public act of worship

indicators.note: taking part in something means being inside it, so the university word goes into the public word

parts.note: common means shared or public, as in common land

explanation.surface: A university takes part in a public religious service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Christian sacrament of shared bread and wine, the Eucharist, is a central act of worship.

clue.text: March around end of town is featured in West End show song

indicators.note: being featured in a show means appearing inside it, so this group goes within the musical's title

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical, a long-running show in London's theatre district, the West End

indicators.note: around means wrapping, so the month abbreviation encloses the final letter of town

parts.note: Mar is the standard abbreviation for the month of March

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A procession circling the edge of town appears in a song from a London musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End show is Lionel Bart's Oliver!, but the song itself comes from a different musical, Show Boat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous bass number from Kern and Hammerstein's musical Show Boat, sung about the Mississippi.

clue.text: Company doctor providing something for nit inspection?

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A company doctor supplies something to check for head lice.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-toothed one is drawn through hair to find and remove lice eggs, called nits.

clue.text: Ray and Maureen, getting on, smile

parts.note: Mo is a common short form of the name Maureen
on means getting on, as in being on the bus
a beam is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Ray and Maureen, a couple getting older, are smiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name partnered with Maureen, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light shining from the moon at night is a ray of reflected sunlight.

clue.text: Group's distance across the water?

definitions.meaning: an alliance or association of clubs or nations
an old unit of length, about three miles, often used at sea

explanation.surface: A team's travelling distance over the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sporting alliance and a measure of roughly three miles used by sailors.

clue.text: Old people blossom with first bit of activity

parts.note: may is hawthorn blossom

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Elderly people bloom once they take up some activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient civilisation of Central America is named after these people, famous for pyramids and a calendar.

clue.text: Notice superior language conveying love and hero-worship

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
U means upper class or superior, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: conveying means carrying within, so the language word holds the zero

parts.note: Latin is the classical language of Rome
love is nil in tennis scoring, so O

explanation.surface: An advertisement in a posh language carrying love and devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'superior' gives U from the old British U and non-U distinction between upper-class and other usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive admiration or flattery directed at someone idolised is the same as worship of a hero.

clue.text: Heather sitting by lake in bra and knickers?

indicators.note: sitting by means placed next to, so the heather comes beside the lake

parts.note: ling is a common species of heather
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather sits by a lake wearing only her underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name but is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's underwear such as bras and knickers is collectively called by this French-derived word.

clue.text: Boat race crew? Didn't eat everything, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the answer sounds like the phrase rather than being spelt like it

parts.note: someone who didn't eat everything only ate some

explanation.surface: A rowing team didn't finish their meal, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford and Cambridge rowing contest, with eight rowers in each crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight, such as the oarsmen in a rowing boat, is this kind of collective.

clue.text: Looking at wildlife? It could be exciting for Asian

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters of for Asian are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A trip to see animals in the wild could be thrilling for someone from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on an expedition to observe animals, typically in Africa, is how one views wildlife.

clue.text: Russian author's escape to the West needing inner impulse

indicators.note: needing an inner part means something must be placed inside it
in an across answer west is leftwards, so the escape word is read backwards

parts.note: a vent is an escape, an outlet for gas or feeling
an urge is an impulse

explanation.surface: A Russian writer defects to the West driven by some inner compulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the West' reverses only because this is an across entry, read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan Turgenev was the nineteenth-century Russian novelist who wrote Fathers and Sons.

clue.text: Dead good joke

parts.note: a one is a joke, as in 'that's a good one'

explanation.surface: A really good joke, told by someone saying dead to mean very.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has passed away is said to be departed, a common euphemism for having died.

clue.text: Game followed by fight and murder

indicators.note: followed by means the next piece comes after

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A match is followed by a brawl and a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: In American gangster slang, to eliminate someone by killing them is to do this.

clue.text: Indian dish unfortunately knocked over by mum

indicators.note: by means beside, so mum comes next to the reversed word

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mum

indicators.note: knocked over means turned upside down, so in an across clue the word is reversed

parts.note: alas expresses regret, meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Mum sadly knocks over a curry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' looks like an adverb describing the accident, but it supplies the word of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiced South Asian curry or spice blend, like chicken tikka masala, goes by this name.

clue.text: A fellow wanting castle ultimately for home

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or fellow

indicators.note: ultimately means at the last, so the final letter of castle is taken

explanation.surface: A man who lacks a castle settles for an ordinary home.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling place, a formal word for where someone lives.

clue.text: Open University set of books dumped in sea — great quantity

indicators.note: dumped in means thrown into, so these letters go inside the sea word

parts.note: main is a poetic word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main
OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: University textbooks are thrown into the ocean in huge numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set of books' is a crossword convention for one of the two Testaments of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a heap or pile of something, as in a backlog of paperwork, means a large amount.

clue.text: Model made of one type of wood

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A model built from a particular kind of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to aspire to is a model, as in a model citizen.

clue.text: Writer's brother squashing the ego

indicators.note: squashing means pressing something in, so the brother holds the self inside

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A writer's sibling crushes his big ego.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpoint pen, named after its inventor László Bíró, is a writing instrument.

clue.text: Don boasted about words written in diary

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters of Don boasted are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university lecturer bragged about entries in his journal.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Pepys famously ended his diary entries with this phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepys closed many daily entries in his seventeenth-century journal with this sign-off before sleeping.

clue.text: Words of contempt never conveyed by Twitter?

indicators.note: conveyed by means carried within, so the poetic never goes inside

parts.note: birds twitter, that is, sing
ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: Insults never sent via a social media platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twitter' wants to be the social media platform but is birdsong, SING.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful, mocking remarks are this kind of derisive talk, used here as a noun.

clue.text: Young singer to quiver, maiden passing out

indicators.note: passing out means leaving, so the maiden letter departs

parts.note: to tremble is to quiver
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A choirboy shakes as a girl faints.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano with a high voice in a choir sings this part.
